engineA2.summary:
Engine A, round 2. I wrote a new exact engine (r2_core.py, r2_graphs.py). Every number is an exact Gaussian rational. There are no floating-point fits.
- Numerators are evaluated in Gaussian-integer arithmetic, with a bound check that keeps every partial sum below 2^52.
- Each graph class is identified by exact Gauss–Jordan elimination over Q(i) on a complete basis of invariant structures, with zero residual required on extra samples.
- A second random seed reproduces every graph class identically.
- Colour is su(2) (orthonormal, structure constants eps_abc). Quartic colour structures are converted to the algebra-independent basis of tr_g(ad ad ad ad) orderings.

Regression: the engine reproduces the round-1 quadratic counterterms exactly (B1 -1, B2 0, B3 9/4, B4 -1, B5 9/4, B6 4, B7 -1).

**T1 (assumption (A))**
- All 11 requested external sets were enumerated graph by graph. The log eps coefficient was obtained from the exact Gaussian moment of the numerator, with per-edge t_e in [eps,infty).
  - Degree-0 graphs: -(1/(n-1)!)(4^m m!)^{-1}(d_k.d_k)^m N with m = n-2.
  - Degree-1 graphs: the same quantity evaluated at the centroid of the Schwinger simplex.
- By degree counting there are no eps^{-1} or eps^{-1/2} pieces in the cubic and quartic sectors. The Spin(6)-odd sets were checked to vanish exactly.
- I re-derived the bracket weights exactly: {Psi,-} acts as a derivation with weights A:2, lambda:4, c:1, A^*:-2, lambda^*:-4, c^*:-1. Hence (Q+{I,-})Psi = {Psi,S}, which multiplies each term of S by the sum of its leg weights.
- In every sector the computed total equals the predicted multiple of the tree vertex.
- The most general fit, beta S + {Psi',S} with independent weights for A|_V, A|_Wperp, lambda and c, has the unique exact solution beta=0, weights (2,2,4,1).
- So the coefficient along the coupling direction vanishes at one loop.

**T2 (quadratic (c, A|_V) sector of the obstruction)**
- The defect graphs are the five special-edge bubbles from (1/2)str(K'(-1)^{|.|}H P(-1)^{|.|}H), with K' = K_eps - K_0. This formula was verified by brute force in 0 dimensions.
- Total of the special-edge graphs: -(9/2)u eps^{-1} int(dc,A|_V) plus a finite part -(27/8)u int(d^*dc,d^*A|_V). There is no log eps term, and all log 2 terms cancel.
- The tree vertex -Q I^CT[eps] contributes +(9/2)u eps^{-1} int(dc,A|_V), so the eps^{-1} part cancels exactly.
- An independent cross-check gives exactly the same eps^{-1} and finite parts. It applies Q to the exact finite parts of all self-energy classes, using QP = K_eps.
- The finite obstruction (27/16)u Q int(d^*A|_V,d^*A|_V) is Q-exact. The finite counterterm (27/16)u int(d^*A|_V,d^*A|_V) added to I^CT[eps] removes it.
- The other quadratic sectors vanish: (c, A|_Wperp) by Spin(6), confirmed by exactly zero numerators; (c, lambda) by Spin(4).
- The cubic sector is open: I reduced it to special-edge triangles and bubbles but did not compute them.

**T3**
- I restated the round-1 coefficients in both normalisations.
- I recomputed the c letter from {Psi,c} = c: -2 in SW(3), +4 in SW(17).

open_issues: T2 cubic sector of the obstruction was not computed. I reduced it to the eps -> 0 limit of special-edge 1PI triangles and bubbles with leg content (c,A|_V,A|_V), (c,A|_Wperp,A|_Wperp), (c,lambda,lambda) and (c,c,A^*|_V). Special-edge bridges cancel, and s I^CT[eps] has no cubic part. The three-edge special-edge region integrals, to second order in external momenta, are not done.

Round 2 used su(2) colour only. Colour factors are traces of products of ad, and su(2) separates the three tr_g(ad ad ad ad) orderings, so the per-ordering coefficients carry over to any simple g. su(3) was not re-run.

For the quartic sets, individual graph classes are not proportional to the tree vertex. They are reported in a colour-pairing x metric-pairing basis with the conversion to tr_g(ad ad ad ad) orderings; only the totals are 8 x tree.

numpy with Accelerate on macOS raises spurious floating-point flags inside matmul. They are silenced. Exactness is guaranteed by the asserted 2^52 bound on |A|@|B| for every product and by integrality and finiteness assertions on every extracted number.

Vertex labels in graph ids (AAA, AAAA, llA, AcAs, cllS, cccS) are code labels. results_r2.json T1.vertex_label_key maps each to its [ESW (31)] term. Formula chains use only dummy Schwinger variables, with no T and no u as a Schwinger symbol.

engineB2.summary:
Engine B, round 2. This is an independent run: I did not read engine_a. Arithmetic is exact throughout, using Gaussian integers with a tracked denominator.

Method B: eps d/deps is computed as the sum over pinned edges (t_e = eps). The pinned graphs are Taylor-expanded in the external momenta. The radial integral is exact, and the angular average is exact on the 24 short roots of F4, which form a spherical 5-design.

Checks done before production runs:
- The new engine reproduces the round-1 omega=1 two-point log coefficients: lambda-lambda 4 and A*-c -1.
- The abstract colour reduction tr_g(M_n...M_1) was compared against explicit su(3) traces in 20 cases, all matching, including the symmetrised quartic adjoint trace and the Jacobi relation.
- A 0-dim Grassmann toy confirmed three things:
  - The round-1 supertrace formula with H_ij = D_i D_j I (D_j applied first) is exact for triangles with odd legs.
  - The transposed Hessian order fails at n=3, although it passes for n<=2.
  - For the odd special edge, the parity operator must act on the kernel's row index.

T1 (all 11 external sets; units u = hbar tr_g(ad_X ad_Y)/((X,Y)16pi^2)):
- Every total log eps coefficient equals exactly the multiple of the tree vertex predicted by assumption (A).
- No graph has an eps^-1 or eps^-1/2 piece.
- In each total, the parity-odd and symmetrised-trace (non-Lie) colour parts cancel.
- Fitting the 15 sectors (4 quadratic, 8 cubic, 3 quartic) with field rescalings plus kappa times S gives the unique solution alpha_A=2, alpha_lambda=-4, alpha_c=-1, kappa=0. The coupling-direction coefficient therefore vanishes at one loop.

T2 (sector with legs c and A|_V):
- The one-loop D_eps graphs are five bubbles, each with one special edge K_eps-K_0 and one P edge, plus the vertex -Q I^CT.
- At eps^-1 the bubbles give -(9/2)u eps^-1 int(A|_V,dc). This cancels exactly against -Q of (9/4)u eps^-1 int(A|_V,A|_V).
- There is no log eps term.
- The finite obstruction is O = -(27/8)u int(d*A|_V, d*dc) = (27/16)u Q int(d*A|_V,d*A|_V). It is Q-exact.
- It is removed by the finite counterterm F = (27/16)u int(d*A|_V,d*A|_V), added to I^CT.
- An independent check gives the same eps^-1 and finite values exactly. That check is the exact eps->0 expansion of the longitudinal regulated self-energy, which equals Q W_1 and uses no special edges.
- The other quadratic sectors, (c,A|_Wperp) and (c,lambda), vanish by R-symmetry and Lorentz covariance.

T3: all round-1 coefficients are restated in both normalisations. The ghost letter c is computed by route (i): -2 in SW(3) and +4 in SW(17).

open_issues: Cubic sector of the one-loop QME obstruction was not computed. It needs three ingredients: triangles and quartic-vertex bubbles with one special edge, the {I, I^CT[eps]}_eps vertex, and the one-particle-reducible graphs -Q I^CT --P-- I. Only a structural statement is given: by s-closure, the cubic part equals (27/16)u{I, int(d*A_V,d*A_V)} (cubic part) plus an s-closed remainder.

In the four-leg sets, individual T1 graphs are not proportional to the tree vertex. They contain the symmetrised adjoint trace (1/24) sum tr_g(ad ad ad ad), in units hbar/16pi^2, which cancels only in each total. Per-graph values are reported as full local structures.

The T3 ghost-letter sign is fixed by consistency with round 1. My direct route-(i) orientation gives +2 for c, alongside +4 for iota_w A and +8 for lambda, which round 1 tabulates as -4 and -8. The tabulated value of -2 inherits the round-1/DEFINITIONS sign convention, whose origin is a global sign between the anomalous part and the tabulated coefficient.

The T2 parity rule for the odd special edge (the parity operator on the kernel row) is established by the 0-dim toy, using two-leg cases only; three-leg cases with K were trivially zero in the toy. T2 needs only two-leg cases, and the rule is also confirmed by the independent self-energy route.
Per-graph ids in T1 are graph classes summed over external-leg assignments and over ghost-loop orientations (Bose-symmetrised).

diagrams2.summary:
Diagrams round 2 is done, covering both parts of the role: the FeynArts census and drawings, and the manuscript composites.

Census and drawings:
- I extended the round-1 drawing model into a new model, N4Draw2. Round-1 files are untouched.
- The new model adds external-only antifield legs (A^*|_{W^perp}, lambda^*, c^*) and the special edge K_eps - K_0, drawn with the grey band, an arrow from field end to antifield end, and the label K_eps - K_0.
- FeynArts 3.12 / FeynCalc 10.2.1 enumerated, at class level:
  - every one-loop 1PI graph with P(eps,infty) edges for the 8 cubic and 3 quartic T1 external sets;
  - every one-loop connected graph with external (c, A|_V) for the T2 QME defect.
- 129 graphs were added to manifest.json with kind 'cubic' (31), 'quartic' (85) and 'qme_defect' (13). Each entry carries:
  - the id `<external>:<vertex types>:<internal lines>`, with #n / #rn suffixes;
  - the FeynArts symmetry factor s and an independently computed |Aut|;
  - the leg assignment at each vertex and an oriented loop cycle;
  - omega, and the graph data.

Checks:
- An independent Python enumeration of labelled-leg one-loop cycles reproduces FeynArts exactly, both per set and per (vertices, lines, s).
- Every one of the 225 drawings (round 1 and round 2) was read back from its TeX and compared with its FeynArts record: the vertex of each external leg, external line style and arrow, and internal style, grey band and arrow. There are no mismatches.

Composites:
- 25 composites with 179 panels are in diagrams/composite/. Each is a PNG at 300 dpi on a white background, with a PDF beside it, and composites.json is written.
- In round-2 and route-(ii) panels the external field legs are labelled field(p_j), where j is the leg number of the id. Without this, channels with identical external fields would look the same.
- Label sizes are measured by LaTeX, and overlaps and label–line clearance were checked and repaired automatically. I also viewed every composite.
- Some panels reuse another graph's FeynArts geometry for a uniform layout, either through a graph isomorphism or by re-styling the lines. composites.json records this per panel, and every final drawing is checked against its own record.

results_r2.json in diagrams/ holds the census in the requested T1/T2 schema. The numerical fields (log_eps, eps_inv, finite, totals, predicted_from_A, verdicts, T3, formula_chains) are null: computing them is the engines' job, not part of this role.
open_issues: Numerical T1/T2/T3 results (per-graph log eps and eps^{-1} coefficients, totals, the assumption (A) test, the T2 obstruction and finite counterterm, the T3 normalisation table, formula_chains) are outside the diagrams role. They are null in diagrams/results_r2.json, to be filled from the engines by graph id.
The '#n' suffix in ids comes from FeynArts output order. If an engine numbers channels differently, match graphs by the manifest fields legs_at_vertices and loop_cycle rather than by '#n'.

Two composites are slightly wider than 6.5 in: quartic_AV2_AWperp2_triangles.png (509.9 bp) and route_ii_Keps.png (507.7 bp). At 6.5 in display width their diagram labels are about 7.4 pt; every other composite fits within 6.5 in.
In quartic_AV4_boxes.png, panels (l) and (o) keep labels slightly closer together than the automatic 2-unit spacing target. I checked both visually: nothing overlaps.

In composites, some panels use another graph's FeynArts geometry (isomorphism templates or re-styling). Every final drawing is checked against its own record, and this is recorded per panel in composites.json under 'drawing'. The per-graph PNGs in diagrams/png/ are FeynArts' own drawings. The round-2 ones now carry field(p_j) leg labels; the round-1 PNGs are unchanged.
The symmetry factors for the T2 graphs treat K_eps - K_0 as an edge species distinct from P. How the 1/2 of (1/2){I,I} combines with the two bracket orderings is for the engines to apply.

 1.3 Pairing and bracket: Def 1.5 (Odd pairing: even member first with sign +); Def 1.6 (K_0, bracket of C07 Lemma 4.3.2, graded symmetry of ESW Def 1.15); Remark 1.7 (overall sign is a convention).
 1.4 The action: Def 1.8 (ESW (31) reduced, Hodge normalisation); Prop 1.9 (coefficient -1/4 is forced by ESW Lemma 3.4; +1/4 and -1/2 fail); free part (1.2); Remark 1.10 (real slice).

Content not sourced, or stated with reduced scope:
(i) The one-loop formula with odd backgrounds has no proof here: Remark 3.22 cites the third-order check, and Prop 3.21 is proved for complex coefficients only.

audits2.summary: Theory audit, round 2. T1 and T2 survive; the chapters contain no sign or normalisation error, but several statements in ch02 and ch03 are stronger than their proofs. I wrote an independent script with standard Feynman-gauge rules: Faddeev–Popov ghosts, 2 Dirac adjoint fermions, and every propagator multiplied by e^{-eps k^2}. It computes the longitudinal one-loop A|_V two-point function exactly. Result: (9/4) eps^{-1} int(A,A) + (27/16) int(d^*A|_V,d^*A|_V) in the unit hbar tr_g(ad_X ad_Y)/((X,Y)16pi^2), with no log. This reproduces the T2 totals (-9/2 eps^{-1}, finite -27/8) and the fermion special-edge row exactly. The log cancellation happens only between the gauge loop and the ghost loop, which checks their relative sign. T1 is consistent with the textbook N=4 Feynman-gauge renormalisation (ratios 4:6:8, no coupling renormalisation), and power counting shows that the computed sectors cover all of one loop. Findings: 5 statements refuted as written, 6 moderate and 11 minor items, each with its gap and a fix.
audits2.key_results:
VERDICTS
(i) T1, assumption (A) and coupling direction: CONFIRMED.
- The log eps part of I^CT[eps] equals (Q+{I,-})(2int(A,A^*) - 4int(lambda^*,lambda) - int(c^*,c)) times the unit times log eps. I rederived this bracket as a weighted field count (A:2, lambda:4, c:1; antifields negative). The signs -4 and -1 arise because lambda^* and c^* are the even members of their pairs.
- The fit is overdetermined and forces the coupling coefficient to 0.
- By power counting, the computed sectors are all local structures at one loop, so (A) holds at one loop and is not only "verified to the extent computed".
- Minor caveats:
  - The coupling direction d/ds S[(1+s)(-,-)] also rescales the BV pairing. It differs from the classical part of S by (Q+{I,-})(-int(c^*,c)), so the fitted coefficient is unchanged.
  - The fit basis has a single lambda weight, but there are two independent chiral lambda terms. The chirality-odd test in the (lambda,lambda,A|_Wperp) set forces the two weights to be equal.
  - For general g the quartic result rests on engine B's exact colour reduction only. Engine A is su(2) only.

(ii) T2, the defect D_eps: CONFIRMED for the quadratic sector, with an independent recomputation.
- The formula D = QJ + 1/2{J,J}_eps + hbar Delta_eps J is correct. With the CME, the order-hbar^0 special edge is K_eps - K_0. The order-hbar terms are Delta_eps I (=0 by colour), -Q I^CT[eps] and -{I,I^CT}_eps (cubic).
- The factor 1/2 and the signs are confirmed because route (a) agrees with route (b), and both agree with my independent self-energy computation.
- The census of graphs is complete.
- Caveats:
  - [moderate] At quadratic order the eps^{-1} cancellation and the absence of log eps are automatic: Q is linear, and I^CT is by construction the singular part of the same two-point function.
  - [moderate] Q-exactness is also automatic here: the only structure in this sector is int(d^*dc,d^*A|_V) = -1/2 Q int(d^*A|_V,d^*A|_V). Adding F changes the cubic obstruction by -{I,F}, so the obstruction is removed only in the quadratic component; the full one-loop QME is OPEN.
  - [minor] F = (27/16) unit int(d^*A|_V,d^*A|_V) is local and allowed. It is a finite order-hbar change of the interaction (I -> I - F), not part of I^CT[eps], which by Thm B is purely singular and unique. F is not special-conformal invariant, so it matters for Step 2.

(iii) Chapters 1–3.
- ch01: confirmed (I re-derived the vertices, Q and the pairing). Minor issues:
  - ch01-1: the third item of Prop c1-cme is false for abelian g. REFUTED as stated; restrict to nonabelian g.
  - ch01-2: the manuscript's Q adjointness is the opposite of [ESW Def 1.16(3)] as printed, and this conflict is not recorded. The ledger resolution X8 says to use the ESW formula; the printed ESW sign would make <A,QA> vanish, so the manuscript's choice is the right one.
- ch02: Prop c2-tower is proven for every g; the d_CE sign lemma and the component signs are confirmed against the ESW text.
  - ch02-1 [moderate, REFUTED as stated]: "super-Jacobi holds on every triple" rests on one random draw per type triple. The bound per draw is up to 3/4 and none is stated. An exhaustive check on a basis is cheap.
  - ch02-2 [minor]: "holds for all seven types" is shown for su(2) at sampled generators only.
- ch03: the core identities are confirmed: QP(eps,infty)=K_eps, the UV-boundary identity (algebra), the homotopy identity, the axiom status ((3),(5) fail; Im Q^GF not isotropic), the propagator and the one-loop formula for complex coefficients.
  - ch03-1 [REFUTED]: "every Q-closed alpha in E_c is Q-exact" is false in E_c. Counterexample: c^* compactly supported with int(c^*,X) != 0.
  - ch03-2 [REFUTED]: "the complex of functionals ... is acyclic" does not follow. Because (Q^GF)^2 != 0, P(0,infty)* does not preserve E_c + P(0,infty)*E_c, so the primitive F o h_(n) is not shown to lie in the same class.
  - ch03-3 [REFUTED]: "every Q-closed functional at scale infinity is Q-exact" is false. Counterexample: e -> int(c^*-component, X) is Q-closed and not Q-exact on E_c.
  - ch03-4 [minor]: no class of functionals is specified on R^4. Volume divergences appear, e.g. Delta_eps int(A,A^*).
  - ch03-5 [minor]: the remark that "obstructions sit on K_eps edges" leaves out the counterterm vertices.
  - ch03-6 [minor]: the one-loop formula is proven only for complex coefficients.
  - ch03-7 [minor]: the adjointness names for Q and Q^GF are the opposite of [C07 §1, §1.1] and [CG2 §7.2.1], and the conflict is not recorded.
open_issues: T2 cubic sector of the one-loop obstruction (special-edge triangles, quartic-vertex bubbles, {I,I^CT}_eps, plus the -{I,F} shift from the finite counterterm) is not computed; (Q+{I,-})-exactness of the full one-loop obstruction is open.

ch03 acyclicity: define a decay-graded space of sections that is stable under Q and P(0,infty)*, and restate Cor c3-functionals and Remark c3-story. Zero-mode classes such as int(c^*,X) are not Q-exact on E_c and must be acknowledged.

ch03 Thm c3-uv / Cor c3-qme: state the class of functionals on R^4 (compactly supported coefficients, or densities modulo total derivatives) so that d_P, d_{K_eps} and Delta_infty = 0 are well defined.

ch02: replace the single-draw super-Jacobi, Killing-form and block-rule checks by exhaustive or symbolic verification. Repeat the arity-1 to 3 equivariant components on a gauge algebra without the su(2) degeneracies, e.g. su(3).
ch03 Prop c3-oneloop: give a proof for coefficients with odd elements, or restrict the statement.

Record two source conflicts in the manuscript: the sign in ESW Def 1.16(3) vs Prop c1-Q, and the C07 'self adjoint' / 'skew self adjoint' naming for Q and Q^GF (ledger X8). Restrict the third item of Prop c1-cme to nonabelian g.

audits2.summary: This round-2 numbers audit recomputed both targets with new exact scripts in qa/audit_numbers2_src. No project code was imported. Conventions were taken only from classical/classical_spec.md: (F_A,F_A) is the Hodge pairing, Q c = -dc, and the components of P(eps,infty). Inside the scripts the propagators were derived again: A-A as the Feynman-gauge covariance, lambda-lambda as (-K)^{-1}, and c-A^*|_V as the pseudo-inverse of (dc,A^*). The one-loop functional is +-(1/2) sum (1/n) Tr[(P V)^n], with V the background quadratic part of I; for two external lambda legs it is the quadratic form <Y G Y> with background-corrected lines. Log eps coefficients were extracted exactly as -(1/(16 pi^2)) times the S^3 average of the degree -4 part of the large-k expansion, which does not depend on the regulator. For T2 every A|_V two-point graph was evaluated exactly with Schwinger parameters on [eps, infty), and the eps -> 0 expansion was done in closed form with the Euler constant and log 2 kept symbolic. The obstruction was then read off as Q of the local longitudinal part of the renormalised functional. In the (c,A|_V) sector, Q kills the transverse part, and (dc, d^*dA) integrates to 0, which removes the (c,A^*) part. Every compared number matches compare_r2.json, and no disagreements were found.
